description: ADR 0033 addendum A (PROTOCOL 8.3, 12.7): a device's introduction key — its ML-KEM-768 sealing key, which its relay keeps — signed by the Ed25519 key its mailbox is the hash of: iks = Ed25519(edSeed, utf8("z-intro-key-v1:") || edPub || SHA-256(ek)), verified by 21.4's one rule; the entry ek || iks a relay keeps and the hint its ready names it by, b64url(SHA-256(entry)[0..16]); FIPS 203 7.2's modulus check at its edges; the acceptance rule a sender applies, each refusal breaking one of its checks; an introduction mailbox's key, kintroSeed = HKDF(introSeed, "z-handle-intro-k-v1", empty, 64); and contact codes carrying sk = SHA-256(ek), an optional member beside pqc that every older reader ignores. No client publishes, fetches or emits any of it before 44.11-44.12.

modulus_check.name: first_coefficient_q_minus_1
modulus_check.why: the first coefficient of t-hat at q - 1, the largest it may be

modulus_check.name: first_coefficient_q
modulus_check.why: the first coefficient at q: ByteDecode12 reduces it to 0, so the round trip differs

modulus_check.name: last_coefficient_4095
modulus_check.why: the last coefficient of the third polynomial at 2^12 - 1

modulus_check.name: rho_changed
modulus_check.why: the last 32 bytes are rho, a seed, and are not checked: another key, well formed

acceptance.name: iks_other_ed
acceptance.why: the linked device's genuine entry served for the root's mailbox: its iks is under another ed

acceptance.name: iks_other_key
acceptance.why: the root's genuine iks served beside another key: it signs another key's hash

acceptance.name: ek_modulus
acceptance.why: a key whose first coefficient is q, signed by the root's own key: only the modulus check refuses it

acceptance.name: iks_s_plus_l
acceptance.why: the genuine signature with S + L: what a lenient verifier takes, and the one rule (21.4) does not

acceptance.name: wrong_mailbox
acceptance.why: the root's genuine entry, checked as the answer for the linked device's mailbox

acceptance.name: sk_mismatch
acceptance.why: another key with an iks the root's key made — what an adversary who forges Ed25519 at the fetch serves: the code's sk refuses it

acceptance.name: sk_mismatch_without_sk
acceptance.why: the same entry for a route with no sk — a list device, a request, a code from an older app: accepted, which is the residual sk exists for

sk_without_pqc.why: sk with pqc and pqcs taken out: refused, not read as a classical code

sk_not_a_string.why: a member of the wrong type
